claim: In adolescent mouse cortex, synapses are about 18% smaller after sleep than after wake (EM: ASI -18.9% vs spontaneous wake, -17.5% vs enforced wake; 6,920 synapses, 12 mice), and synaptic AMPA receptors fall in sleep (GluA1/GluA2 in PSD, about 20% of PSD proteins regulated). Sleep as net down-scaling of synaptic strength is supported in this population.
agent_test: Add-only lesson store vs store plus a scheduled prune pass over the whole store; same total tokens; measure held-out task accuracy and store size.

claim: The down-scaling result does not generalise cleanly: juvenile rat cortex shows stable mEPSC amplitudes and stable thalamocortical responses across sleep and wake (Cary and Turrigiano 2021); cats show evoked responses rising after sleep (Chauvette 2012); hippocampus CA1 results point both ways (Spano 2019 larger ASI after wake; Havekes 2016 fewer spines after sleep deprivation); adult mice show no sleep/wake spine change. The effect depends on age, species, region and readout.
agent_test: None directly. Lesson for design: do not assume one prune rate fits all stores; test prune benefit separately on young (few lessons) and mature (many lessons) stores.

claim: Sleep also strengthens or adds synapses selectively, not only weakens: new spines form on specific branches after learning (15.3% vs 4.4-6.4%), V1 response potentiation after patterned experience needs sleep, and REM prunes new spines while keeping some. SHY must be read as net renormalisation plus selective strengthening, so a prune-only memory pass is a poor analogy.
agent_test: Compare prune-only vs prune plus consolidate (merge surviving lessons into one rule) vs add-only at equal tokens.

claim: Which synapses shrink is disputed. de Vivo 2017: about 80% (small and medium) scale down, the largest ~20% and those without recycling endosomes are spared (small/medium -11.9%, large +0.7%). Diering 2017 as summarised by Tononi and Cirelli: large spines shrank most. The authors' later review lists the two as in disagreement.
agent_test: Test prune order: remove smallest/least-used lessons first vs largest/most-used first; protect-big is the SHY-consistent rule from de Vivo.

claim: Down-regulation is gated by state and activity: firing-rate set-point return after a perturbation happened during sleep not wake in rat V1 (firing +114% on ER2, back to +2% by ER4; 30 of 36 neurons), opposite to Hengen 2016 where upward recovery needed wake. Watson 2016 found NREM lowered fast cells but raised slow ones (homogenisation). Direction and mechanism differ across studies; the shared point is that regulation is state-gated.
agent_test: Not directly testable. Analogy: run consolidation only in a separate offline phase, not during task steps (test: inline pruning vs offline pruning at equal tokens).

claim: Protection from depression for the active or reactivated: units most active in sleep are spared. Gulati 2017: indirect units fell about 32% in task peak firing after sleep while direct units rose about 7%, and blocking cortical ON/UP states stopped both. Gonzalez-Rueda 2018 (anaesthetised mouse): UP states depress by default (mean 63-71%) but pre-post paired synapses are protected. Computer models (Nere 2013) use the same rule.
agent_test: Prune rule A: decay unless the lesson was retrieved and used in a successful step (reinforced) vs rule B: decay by age only. Equal tokens, same store cap.

claim: Human indirect evidence supports a wake-up, sleep-down cycle of net synaptic strength: after one night of sleep deprivation (N=20, within-subject) less TMS intensity was needed and LTP-like plasticity fell (Condition F(1,19)=7.5, p=0.013, partial eta2 0.283); frontal TMS slope rose across 18 h of wake and returned after sleep (Huber 2012, via review). All indices are indirect and motor-cortex based.
agent_test: None direct. Background support for the saturation argument: a store that only grows loses learning room (retrieval noise).

claim: Models of sleep down-selection with protection-from-depression raise signal-to-noise and recall: procedural recall 80% to 90%, S/N 4 to 9 after one sleep, 95% and S/N 19 later; wake-only potentiation or potentiation in sleep drops recall to 20-25% with S/N 0. Declarative model recall first falls (87% to 75%) but beats wake-only (53%) and recovers to 94% after 10 cycles. All toy networks.
agent_test: Multi-cycle test: measure accuracy after 1, 3 and 10 prune cycles; expect an early dip then gain.

claim: Dose-response is an inverted U: too much down-scaling or sleep hurts. Zeroing the smallest 75% of weights was the best level in class-incremental CIFAR-100 (p<=0.5 looked like 0, higher p fell); in STDP spiking nets the best sleep was 10-20% of training and accuracy fell above; napping accuracy peaked at brief naps then fell monotonically with duration.
agent_test: Sweep prune fraction (0, 25, 50, 75, 90% of lessons dropped by lowest score) at equal total tokens; look for an interior optimum.

claim: In neural-network continual learning, sleep-like down-scaling plus local replay is a partial fix and is beaten by a small stored rehearsal buffer; the combination is best. Incremental MNIST: sequential 19.49, sleep (SRC) 48.47, rehearsal 0.75% 79.91, rehearsal+SRC 86.47, OWM 77.04. iCaRL K=100 65.5 to 78.1 with SRC. SIESTA (wake output layer only, sleep replay rest) reached 83.59 top-5 on ImageNet-1K vs 83.31 offline. Wake-sleep consolidated learning also beat replay baselines (CIFAR-10 buffer 200: ER 48.76 to 51.86).
agent_test: Arm: raw episodes kept (small buffer) vs distilled rules only vs both. Equal tokens in the prompt.

claim: Down-scaling without replay does not protect old knowledge: without generative replay accuracy collapsed at every prune fraction p in class-incremental CIFAR-100; freezing 1% of task-1 weights let task 2 be learned but did not preserve task 1. Pruning and replay do different jobs; pruning needs something to replay.
agent_test: Ablation: prune without a replay/retrieval path vs prune plus retrieval of kept lessons.

claim: In LLM agents, deleting low-utility memory records can match or beat add-only stores at a fraction of the size. Xiong 2025: history-based deletion EHRAgent 38.67 to 42.06 (1012 to 784 records), CIC-IoT 85.40 to 89.60, AgentDriver 51.00 to 51.81; combined deletion cut to 188-323 records with small loss; periodic deletion RegAgent 70.95 (2938) to 67.65 (949). Mem0 (ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP): over 90% fewer tokens at near full-context accuracy. RSPM: 30.6% fewer entries with +9.1 solve rate (simulation). FadeMem: 45% less storage with small margin over Mem0. Gap search: Xiong strict-evaluator utility deletion with a 66-79% record cut cost 0-4 points on three agents; under a hard capacity cap equal to the starting store (100 or 180 records) it still beat the fixed store; and history-based deletion beat an error-free memory on AgentDriver.
agent_test: Main test: add-only vs delete-by-utility at equal tokens, on a multi-episode task stream; report accuracy and store size.

claim: Pruning only helps with a reliable utility signal. Xiong 2025: with weak coarse evaluators history-based deletion did not help and errors propagate via experience-following; ACE: weak without ground truth or execution feedback, can be polluted; Dynamic Cheatsheet: small models fill memory with wrong strategies and gain little. Gap search: a judge fine-tuned on only 300 labelled outcomes moved Xiong's coarse evaluator from harmful to useful (AgentDriver 36.92 to 47.37, add-all 32.32); ACE kept its gain with one corrupted reflector update in five (76.1 vs base 70.7) but fell to 66.7 when every update was corrupted. No threshold on judge accuracy has been measured.
agent_test: Run the prune pass with (a) verified outcomes, (b) self-judged outcomes, (c) no outcomes; compare. Matches the guardrail on external verification.

claim: Wholesale LLM rewriting of the memory causes collapse; small delta edits with counters and dedupe avoid it. ACE on AppWorld: context fell from 18,282 tokens to 122 tokens at one step and accuracy fell from 66.7 to 57.1, below the 63.7 no-adaptation baseline. Gap search: ACE ablation, whole-context rewrite style updating 67.3/46.4 vs incremental updates 76.2/64.3 (average 56.9 vs 70.3, ReAct 53.3). Dynamic Cheatsheet separately saw its curator write stubs like 'previous content preserved' instead of rewriting.
agent_test: Arm: full rewrite of lesson file each cycle vs incremental ADD/EDIT/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE edits.

claim: Gist compression loses specifics unless told to keep them. Sleep-style gist summaries beat truncation on multi-hop but dropped dates (temporal-expression preservation 3.05% to 62.39% after one prompt sentence; named entities barely changed). Matches the model result that top-level gist is protected and detail is depressed.
agent_test: When distilling lessons to rules, check for lost conditions (when, which version, which input range); add a keep-conditions instruction and compare.

claim: Reinforcement-count removal (ExpeL: upvote/downvote, remove at score 0) with both insights and retrieved trajectories beats either alone on some domains (HotpotQA insights-only 36% vs retrieve-only 31%; ALFWorld 50 vs 55). Which memory type helps depends on domain; ExpeL gives no pruning ablation. Gap search: ExpeL ablation found insights from few-shot examples alone gave no gain over ReAct and adding reflections to insight extraction hurt; the removal-at-zero rule itself is still not ablated.
agent_test: Run ExpeL-style vote-and-remove vs keep-all with identical retrieval.

claim: Offline sleep-time work before the question (precompute, anticipate) cuts test-time compute about 5x at equal accuracy and gives up to +13% / +18% with scaling; gain tracks how predictable the query is. This is the replay side, not down-selection. At high test budgets plain test-time compute wins.
agent_test: Equal-token arm: tokens spent in an offline consolidation pass vs same tokens at answer time.

claim: LLM-branded sleep memory papers (SCM, SleepGate, ZenBrain, RSPM, FadeMem) report large gains but on synthetic or self-built benchmarks by single groups: SCM 22 facts and 50 noise items; SleepGate a 793K-parameter transformer on synthetic tokens; ZenBrain simulated corpora; RSPM a difficulty-calibrated simulation. None has an independent replication on a real LLM agent task stream. Gap search: RSPM is a short single-group paper with a simulated SWE-bench arm and a reported 19.5-point loss on one hard conversation; FadeMem ablation is the authors' own bar chart.
agent_test: Replicate the cheapest one (RSPM-style sleep every 10 tasks) on a real task stream at equal tokens before adopting any number.

claim: Decay-only forgetting (recency/time decay that only lowers rank, never deletes) has no ablation support in LLM agent work: Generative Agents ranks by decayed recency, MemoryBank uses Ebbinghaus-style R=exp(-t/S), neither tested the decay rule alone. In the toy SleepGate study a decay-only baseline stayed below 18%. Gap search: SleepGate decay-only 7.5% at depth 10 vs trained gate 97.0% (toy model); Reflexion's 1-3 item FIFO window is the common deployed cap and was never ablated.
agent_test: Arm: time-decay ranking vs utility-based deletion at equal tokens.

claim: Why sleep and not wake for renormalisation: wake input is a narrow biased sample, so pruning during a task would favour recent experience; sleep activity samples the whole store. A prune pass over the whole lesson store, not only lessons touched by the current task, avoids recency bias. Conceptual argument, not tested.
agent_test: Prune pass over all lessons vs prune only lessons retrieved in the current task.

claim: Down-scaling depends on local crowding and signal competition: dendrites with fewest synapses scaled down most (-36.4% vs +7.8%, interaction p=0.038, modest), and a neuron whose inputs all come from one source cannot compete, so down-selection fails.
agent_test: Weak test: prune harder in sparse topic areas of the store than dense ones.

claim: SHY was narrowed after criticism to function, not mechanism, which makes it harder to falsify. Critics (Frank 2012) cite temperature and glucocorticoids as alternative causes; supporters answer that slow-wave activity is a good sensor of need.
agent_test: None.

claim: An add-everything lesson store is not neutral: it can be worse than a tiny fixed store and worse than no memory. Xiong 2025: add-all RegAgent 55.48 (4100 records) vs fixed 67.53 (100 records); AgentDriver 32.32 vs 40.11; CIC-IoT 59.90 vs 71.50. Dynamic Cheatsheet: GPT-4o on AIME 2024 baseline 20.0%, full-history append 6.7%, curated DC-RS 40.0%.
agent_test: Arm A add-all, arm B frozen small seed set, arm C curated store; equal total tokens.

claim: When outcomes are known, deleting by outcome-linked utility beats deleting by retrieval frequency or age. Xiong 2025 strict evaluator, periodic (frequency) vs history-based (utility): RegAgent 67.65 vs 69.80, EHRAgent 38.59 vs 42.06, AgentDriver 50.94 vs 51.81, CIC-IoT 80.80 vs 89.60. One paper, four agents, ground-truth evaluator; with coarse judges the ordering is unstable.
agent_test: Prune by mean outcome of runs that used a lesson vs prune by use count vs prune by age, same store size.

claim: Failure-triggered pruning fails when the task is simply hard. RSPM: a LoCoMo conversation with a 35% error rate triggered 21 sleep cycles, pruned 43% of the store and ended 19.5 points below baseline, because a memory used in a failed run was assumed to have caused the failure. A keyword conflict detector (79.5%) was worse than RAG (80.6%); an LLM detector reached 92.5%.
agent_test: Cap the fraction pruned per cycle; require a lesson to fail on tasks where other runs succeed before demoting it.

claim: No numeric threshold exists for how reliable the utility signal must be, but two data points bound it. A judge fine-tuned on 300 labelled outcomes was enough to turn Xiong's add step from harmful to helpful. ACE kept +5.4 with one corrupted update in five, and lost 4.0 points with every update corrupted. Pure self-judging with no outcome signal degrades (ACE finance, Dynamic Cheatsheet).
agent_test: Sweep the share of wrong utility labels (0, 10, 20, 50%) fed to the prune pass; find where store-pruned falls below add-only.

claim: Prune trigger size and dedup strictness are weak knobs at ACE's scale. FiNER base 70.7: pruning when the context passes 10K / 50K / 100K tokens gave 78.6 / 78.4 / 78.3; dedup threshold 50 / 70 / 90% gave 77.0 / 73.9 / 78.6; ten reflection rounds (65.2) did worse than five (67.6) on AppWorld. No interior optimum for store size was found; the prune fraction question is open.
agent_test: Sweep prune fraction (0, 10, 30, 60, 90% per cycle) on stores of 20, 100, 500 lessons.

claim: Use-count and attention-based retention keep stale entries when old values are the ones read most. SleepGate toy study: H2O (highest cumulative attention) reached 7.5% at 2 prior updates, decay-only 12.5%, trained supersession gate 99.0%; the gate collapsed past about 15 near-identical entries (73.5 at n=15, 16.5 at n=30).
agent_test: Include a supersession check (newer lesson contradicts older) in the prune pass, not only use count.

claim: Online (in-task) vs offline (separate pass) memory building has no direct pruning test. Indirect: Agent Workflow Memory offline and online gave similar in-domain results (cross-task step SR 45.1 vs 43.6) and online was better under task mismatch (cross-domain 35.5 vs 32.6), but AWM adds without deleting and success rates are low.
agent_test: Arm: prune each episode during the run vs one prune pass over the whole store after N episodes.

claim: Prune-only vs prune-plus-merge is not isolated anywhere. Indirect: ACE incremental edits and dedupe added about 13 points over a rewrite-style update (70.3 vs 56.9 average); FadeMem removing fusion cost 53.7% of multi-hop F1 (29.43 to 13.63) but that is the authors' bar chart; RSPM gives no prune-only arm. No test of what merged rules lose.
agent_test: Arms: delete only, delete plus merge into rules, merge only; equal tokens; check lost conditions.

claim: Independent replication of the 2026 LLM sleep-memory papers (RSPM, SCM, SleepGate, ZenBrain) was not found. The older, better-run papers (Xiong 2025, ACE, Dynamic Cheatsheet) are not sleep-branded but test the same operations and give the usable numbers. A literature search could not be run in this pass because search and API budgets were exhausted.
agent_test: Replicate one operation (delete by utility) on a public agent benchmark with real model calls.
